title: Context Assembly as the Controlled Variable: A Control-Theoretic View of Harness Policies for Frozen LLM Agents

images.desc:
3 Stability


We use stability in the sense of Zhang and others (2026): a controller is stable over
a window if expected reward is non-decreasing (up to noise) as more episodes accrue, i.e. the controller is making real progress rather than oscillating or diverging. This is a much
weaker (and more directly measurable, from an online learning trace) claim than Lyapunov
asymptotic stability (Khalil, 2002), and it is the right notion for an online bandit/RL
controller whose ”state” is a set of learned weights rather than a physical system with
continuous dynamics.



Definition 1 (Empirical stability).


A controller trained online for TT episodes is δ\delta-stable over window ww if, for all
t≥wt\geq w, the windowed mean reward R¯t=1w​∑i=t−wtRi\bar{R}_{t}=\frac{1}{w}\sum_{i=t-w}^{t}R_{i} satisfies
R¯t≥R¯t−w−δ\bar{R}_{t}\geq\bar{R}_{t-w}-\delta.




Proposition 1 (Informal).


For the ϵ\epsilon-greedy bandit with optimistic initialization
(Paper 2, Sec. 5, cold-start fix), the expected windowed reward is non-decreasing in
expectation once every action has been sampled at least once, because (a) the greedy branch
always selects a non-decreasing running estimate of the best-known action’s value, and (b)
the ϵ\epsilon-exploration branch contributes bounded variance that shrinks as O​(1/n)O(1/\sqrt{n})
with the count nn of samples per action. For REINFORCE, the same claim holds under the
standard policy-gradient assumption of a decaying or sufficiently small learning rate, via
the moving-average-baseline variance reduction already in our implementation
(Paper 2, Sec. 3.4).



We ran a dedicated instrumented experiment (scripts/run_stability_experiment.py):
bandit and REINFORCE, tool-use domain, Ollama qwen2.5:7b, 2 seeds each, 60 episodes/run
(240 episodes total), logging per-episode reward, correctness, and the selection-time
confidence defined below. Figure 1 plots the windowed (15-episode) mean
reward per seed.


Figure 1: Windowed mean reward vs. episode for the bandit and REINFORCE controllers
(2 seeds each; shaded band = min/max across seeds).


The empirical result does not confirm the proposition at this episode budget, and
we report that directly. A per-seed linear fit of reward against episode index gives
slopes of −0.0045-0.0045 and +0.0005+0.0005 per episode for the two bandit seeds, and −0.0024-0.0024 and
−0.0008-0.0008 for the two REINFORCE seeds – three of four runs trend slightly negative,
not non-decreasing, over 60 episodes. We do not read this as a failure of the informal
proposition’s logic so much as confirmation that 60 episodes is far too few for its
asymptotic premise (every action sampled enough for its running estimate to concentrate) to
hold on a 729-action space: this is the same Ω​(M)\Omega(M)-sample regime identified in
Majumdar (2026) and empirically confirmed from the other direction in our
companion Paper 2 (Sec. 5), where 300 episodes – 5×\times this stability run’s budget –
was still not enough for the same controllers to close the gap to a static
DSPy-optimized baseline. Both papers’ empirical sections independently point at the same
bottleneck: our six-lever, 729-configuration action space is large relative to any episode
budget achievable in practical (single-day, single-machine) experimentation, and both the
sample-efficiency and the empirical-stability results we can currently report should be read
as characterizing the under-sampled regime, not the asymptotic one the formal literature
this section engages with typically targets.

4 Uncertainty calibration


A controller that is confident when it is right and unsure when it is wrong is more useful
in the agentic-RPA human-escalation setting (Paper 2, Sec. 6, Recipe step 7) than one whose
confidence is uninformative, even at matched accuracy: escalation to a human is only useful
if low confidence actually predicts a wrong or unverifiable outcome. We report this
directly, rather than assuming it, following the calibration methodology of
Guo et al. (2017).


We define confidence at selection time as the softmax-normalized score of the chosen action
under πϕ\pi_{\phi}: for REINFORCE this is exactly πϕ​(Ct∣xt)\pi_{\phi}(C_{t}\mid x_{t}), the sampling
probability of the action actually taken; for the bandit it is a softmax over
Qϕ​(xt,⋅)Q_{\phi}(x_{t},\cdot) evaluated at the same features (Sec. 2), reported for calibration
purposes only – it does not affect the ϵ\epsilon-greedy selection rule itself. We bin
episodes by confidence decile and compute the Expected Calibration Error,
ECE=∑bnbN​|acc​(b)−conf​(b)|\mathrm{ECE}=\sum_{b}\frac{n_{b}}{N}\left|\text{acc}(b)-\text{conf}(b)\right|.


Figure 2: Reliability diagram: controller confidence (softmax score of the chosen action)
vs. realized success rate, by decile. ECE = 0.607.


ECE = 0.607 – a large number, and an instructive one. On the same 240-episode run,
mean confidence was 0.00140.0014 (bandit) and 0.00140.0014 (REINFORCE) against a realized success
rate of 0.640.64 and 0.580.58 respectively – confidence and accuracy differ by roughly two
orders of magnitude, not a small miscalibration. The mechanism is direct, not a training
failure: softmax probability over M=729M{=}729 near-equally-scored actions is bounded near
1/M≈0.00141/M\approx 0.0014 whenever the score distribution has not yet concentrated (which,
per Sec. 3, it has not at 60 episodes), while task success is a
per-episode binary outcome with a base rate set by the task and model, not by MM. These two
quantities live on incompatible scales by construction, and comparing them directly – as a
naive implementation of the Recipe 7 human-escalation rule (Paper 2, §6) would – produces
an escalation signal that is uninformative: essentially every episode looks ”low
confidence” under the raw softmax score, regardless of whether the episode in fact
succeeded. Practical implication: raw action-selection probability over a
large discrete harness space is not usable as an escalation-confidence signal without
recalibration (e.g. temperature scaling fit on held-out episodes, or defining confidence
via the bandit’s estimated value margin between the top two actions rather than a softmax
over the full space) – a correction we flag here for RECIPE.md rather than
silently build in, since it is a genuine open design point, not a solved one.
